content:
Claude is upgrading the Chrome sidebar into a full Cowork session, enabling work and conversations in the browser to flow seamlessly across Claude's other apps.

Browser work now carries across all Claude apps

Anthropic announced the change today. Conversations started from the sidebar now save to the Claude conversation history, letting users pick them up in the Claude desktop, web, and mobile apps.

Already-configured account Skills and connectors work in the browser without additional setup. Claude in Chrome can read the current page and take actions using the user's existing logged-in browser sessions, including clicking links, converting pages, typing text, and filling forms.

Anthropic's example: ask Claude to gather invoice data from multiple vendor portals, build a spreadsheet, then continue the same session on desktop to add local files or compare the results with historical budgets.

The update closes a gap in Claude's browser workflow. Previously, sidebar sessions were entirely siloed from conversations in Claude's other apps, with no way to carry the content or context over.

Anthropic previously introduced an in-app browser in Claude Code, which uses a separate profile. By contrast, the Chrome extension can operate directly on sites where the user is already logged in.

Anthropic cautions that browser agents remain vulnerable to prompt injection attacks.

An extra safeguard reviews actions with major impact under auto-approve mode; for things like purchases or sharing personal data, Claude still asks first.

The company says these measures reduce but do not eliminate risk.

Availability

The Cowork sidebar is available starting today for Max and Team customers, with a phased rollout to Pro users over the coming weeks. Enterprise admins can enable the feature and restrict access to approved domains. Claude in Chrome is not yet supported on other Chromium browsers or mobile devices.

The release is part of Anthropic's ongoing push to make Claude workflows seamless across platforms.

Recent additions include Claude Code for Mac adding iOS app live previews, and new manipulation options in Opus 4.8 to support longer-running work across more products and devices.
